cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: WiFi ≠ cable – a wireless way to connect computers and phones to the internet.

p.em: Example: Our home WiFi works in every room.

cosy-blockquote.p: Signal ≠ silence – waves that carry information through the air.

p.em: Example: The WiFi signal gets weak near the balcony.

cosy-blockquote.p: Router ≠ computer – a device that sends internet signals to your devices.

p.em: Example: Restart the router if the internet stops working.

cosy-blockquote.p: Wall ≠ door – a vertical side of a room.

p.em: Example: WiFi signals can pass through wooden walls.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identify ≠ confuse – to recognize who someone is.

p.em: Example: A phone can identify your face to unlock.

cosy-blockquote.p: Walk ≠ run – to move on foot at a regular pace.

p.em: Example: Each person has a unique way they walk.

cosy-blockquote.p: Secret ≠ public – something that is kept hidden from others.

p.em: Example: Keep your personal WiFi password secret.

cosy-blockquote.p: Smart ≠ basic – having or showing intelligence or computer technology.

p.em: Example: Smart homes use WiFi to turn on lights.

cosy-blockquote.p: Safe ≠ dangerous – not in danger or likely to be hurt.

p.em: Example: We want our personal data to be safe.

cosy-blockquote.p: Test ≠ ignore – to examine something to see if it works.

p.em: Example: Scientists tested the new WiFi system in an office.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Do you use wireless WiFi or a cable connection at home?
★ Is your internet connection fast and reliable?

How strong is the internet signal in your bedroom or kitchen?
★ Have you ever lost WiFi signal in an emergency?

Where is your home internet router placed?
★ Do you know how to restart a router when the connection drops?

Can WiFi waves pass through a thick concrete wall easily?
★ Does your home have dead zones with no signal?

How can smart technology identify a person by their movement patterns?
★ Are you surprised that radio waves can map human shapes?

How far do you walk every day during your normal routine?
★ Do you count your daily walking steps on a phone?

Why should you keep your private passwords and PIN codes a secret?
★ How often do you change your WiFi password?

What smart devices do you have in your house?
★ Do you use voice assistants like Alexa or Siri?

Is it safe to connect to public free WiFi networks in cafes?
★ Do you use public internet when traveling?

How do engineers test new internet technologies before releasing them?
★ Do you like trying new tech gadgets?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Using WiFi signals to track human movement inside buildings is a great innovation. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you like smart lights that detect when you enter a room?

A strong internet signal in every public place should be a basic city service. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Is free public WiFi available in your city?

Replacing old home router hardware every three years improves digital security. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How old is your home router?

Signals passing through a bedroom wall raise serious privacy concerns. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Does indoor spatial tracking feel intrusive?

Technology that can identify individuals without their knowledge should be strictly regulated. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Are you worried about stealth surveillance?

Encouraging people to walk more can be helped by smart tracking apps. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do fitness apps motivate you to exercise?

Keeping your home network password a secret is the most important security rule. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you share your home WiFi with visitors?

Every modern home will eventually become a fully automated smart home. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do smart appliances make life easier or more complicated?

It is never safe to send personal banking details over public WiFi. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you use a VPN on public networks?

Scientists should test all surveillance technology for privacy risks before sale. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should tech ethics boards inspect new inventions?

ul.li: Incorrect: WiFi can to see people. → Correct: WiFi can see people. ((Modal 'can' takes base verb without 'to'.))
Incorrect: It recognize my walked. → Correct: It recognizes my walk / gait. ((3rd person singular present tense 'recognizes', and use noun 'walk'.))
